headline: You cleared your own board this afternoon — Seth B. called AND put in writing at 1:38, the draft queue emptied 9 to 3 in twenty-five minutes, and the 355 preview read finally answered at 3:44 · DO: chase Angela B.'s read on 355 tonight while the house is fresh · WATCH: the lead webhook is still dead at 55+ hours, three days with no instant responder.

notes: ✅ THE FLEET CAME BACK AND STAYED BACK. Eight routines have run clean since this morning with ZERO blocked lines — the milestone engine four times (11:03, 2:03, 5:03 and the earlier gap scan), two Delta passes, the engagement run and the weekly CEO Sweep at 5:25. The 26-hour dark window that dominated the midday board is closed and did not reopen. Sunday still ran thin at 8 heartbeat lines against 40-plus on a weekday, but thin-because-it-is-Sunday is a different thing from dark.

🛑 ONE ROUTINE IS STILL GENUINELY DEAD AND IT IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE. The Brivity instant-lead webhook has been deactivated since Friday 9:32 AM — now past 55 hours — and the instant responder has written ZERO heartbeat lines for three straight days. That is why this panel reads alert rather than ok: no BLOCKED line exists because the routine cannot run to write one. Today's CEO Sweep proved it three independent ways and raised it as a p1. ⚠️ DO NOT SIMPLY SWITCH IT BACK ON — 243 errors in five minutes is what deactivated it, and flipping it will storm again. Read the execution log first.

⭐ THE HUMAN OUTRAN THE MACHINE TODAY, WHICH IS WORTH SAYING PLAINLY. Between 1:15 and 1:40 you sent eight emails — every draft the Delta had staged, plus both Burnham briefs and the Seth Berry update — then the Land Bank inquiry at 3:02. The queue this board has been nagging about for a week went from nine to three in twenty-five minutes. The lesson the fleet should take: staging work is inert, surfacing it is the cheap half that makes it move.

callBlock.who: The dead lead webhook — three days with nothing answering new leads (ops, not a person)
callBlock.why: 🛑 THE WEEK'S BIGGEST LEAK AND THE ONLY THING ON THIS BOARD THAT IS STILL ACTIVELY BLEEDING. The Brivity instant-lead scenario has been off since Friday 9:32 AM — past 55 hours — and it is the instant responder's ONLY input as well as the first rung of the ownership check. Every lead that arrived this weekend arrived to silence. ⚠️ THE PART THAT SHOULD BOTHER YOU MOST IS NOT THE OUTAGE, IT IS THE SILENCING: a p1 raised this correctly on Friday and it was checked off Saturday morning with the scenario still dead. The alarm was answered by closing the alarm. ⭐ THREE INDEPENDENT RECEIPTS AGREE: the stop notice sat unread 55 hours, roughly 200 junk alerts fired in one minute then nothing, and the responder's heartbeat went from 6-13 lines a day to zero. ⛔ DO NOT JUST FLIP IT ON — 243 errors in five minutes reads like a payload or mapping change, and that storm is what killed it. Open the execution history first, or it deactivates itself again within the hour.

callBlock.who: Cheryl G. — the appointment is settled, but the list she asked for four days ago never went out
callBlock.why: ✅ NOTHING IS OWED ON THE APPOINTMENT AND THAT AMBIGUITY IS FULLY DEAD. She cancelled Saturday night in her own words, you answered at 10:24 this morning asking for another day, and the ball is legitimately in her court on scheduling. ⭐ WHAT IS STILL OWED IS OLDER AND IT IS THE THING THAT ACTUALLY MOVES HER. On 7/29 she pivoted to Mt Laurel, not much above $600,000, and you answered "will start working on that now — any must haves?" That question has hung since Wednesday and the Mt Laurel list has never gone out. She just cancelled a showing on a house she found herself; two or three real Mt Laurel options is what makes the rebook happen instead of waiting on her to raise her hand a third time. ⚠️ Her own behaviour supports the number — average view price is well above what she stated, so the $600K ceiling is softer than she said. ⚠️ NOBODY HAS EVER ASKED whether her own house has to sell first, and that single question changes what you send her.

callBlock.who: David C. — the machine's email promised him a call, and that promise is now three days old
callBlock.why: 🔥 AN UNKEPT SAME-DAY PROMISE MADE IN YOUR NAME, NOW SLIPPED PAST A FULL WEEKEND. He registered Friday morning off the 1709 Fieldstone ad, the responder wrote him at 2:16 PM, and that email says you'll call him. Two emails out, zero replies back. ⚠️ ON A FIRST TOUCH THIS IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE KIND OF MISS, because the broken promise is the only impression he has of you. ⚠️ THE CHEAP EXCUSE FOR THE CALL HAS EXPIRED — the open house on the exact listing he came through ran Saturday and he was never invited. What's left is the honest version: a plain call about what he's actually hunting for. ⭐ AND THERE IS A GENUINELY GOOD REASON TO DIAL HIM TONIGHT — that same listing has a buyer walking it tomorrow at 12:45, so the house he raised his hand about is visibly moving. ⭐ Ownership was verified the hard way, read live in the leads index rather than inferred from a webhook verdict, so this is genuinely yours. ⚠️ No text has gone out; his person page wedged when the sweep tried.

callBlock.who: Sondra & Darrell S. — a buy and a list in one message, and the ball has been in her court since Friday
callBlock.why: 🔥 STILL THE CLEANEST AT-BAT ON THE BOARD AND IT IS BOTH SIDES OF A DEAL. Friday 5:02 PM, unprompted, off an automated listing alert: "We are very interested in this property! I think we are about ready to put ours on the market also! If you have time, we would love to get with you ASAP." ✅ You answered yourself at 5:33 and copied Darrell exactly as she asked. ⚠️ BUT THAT REPLY PUTS THE NEXT MOVE ON HER AND SHE ASKED FOR THE OPPOSITE. She used the word ASAP and already said she's ready; a standing offer is not a calendar invite, and it is now three days old with nothing back. ⭐ THE CALL PROPOSES A SPECIFIC TIME and does both sides in one trip: walk the Helena house she flagged, then walk theirs. The buy side is the two-bathroom setup they told you in March they needed. ⚠️ CALL, DO NOT TEXT — the record shows Agent Referral as the source, so there is no consent trail for a text.

callBlock.who: Jean M. — she raised her hand on Fieldstone Saturday morning and still nothing has answered her
callBlock.why: 🔴 SHE ARRIVED SATURDAY 9:06 AM ASKING ABOUT THE EXACT LISTING WHOSE OPEN HOUSE RAN THAT AFTERNOON, AND THE OPEN HOUSE CAME AND WENT WITHOUT HER. Three separate notifications carried her in, all naming the 1709 Fieldstone ad. ⭐ THE GOOD NEWS IS THE EXCUSE REGENERATED ITSELF: that listing just booked its second-ever showing for tomorrow at 12:45, so the house she asked about is demonstrably moving — that is a far better call than an apology for a missed open house. ⚠️ THE OLD DRAFT IS A HAZARD, NOT A FOLLOW-UP — it invites her to Saturday's event and must not be sent as written. ⚠️ RULE 0 — ownership is NOT hard-verified. The notification renders "Agent: Gene Darden," and that line is not an assignment. Precedent runs your way twice over on this exact campaign, but precedent is not a read. 🛑 SHE IS THE NAMED COST OF THE DEAD WEBHOOK — the instant-lead scenario has been off since Friday morning, so nothing auto-answered her.

callBlock.who: Jake & Leslie J. — the equity email you sent Saturday hard-bounced, and a live channel nobody has tried
callBlock.why: ⚠️ THE MESSAGE DID NOT REACH THEM AND NOTHING IN YOUR OUTBOX WOULD TELL YOU THAT. Saturday 7:40 AM the equity note went out; 47 seconds later Microsoft rejected it permanently — the recipient no longer exists on the school system. The call chip that paired with the draft was already checked off, so the bounce had no surviving owner and you'd have gone into the week believing they had it in writing. ✅ THE GOOD NEWS IS A CLEAN CHANNEL: their record carries a second, personal email that has never once been used — zero messages to it in either alias, all-time — plus a working phone. ⭐ Rule 9 says a bounce becomes a call, and after twelve years as past clients the phone is the better instrument anyway. ⚠️ The equity email opens by claiming a phone attempt that cannot be verified from here, which is exactly why it was not simply re-sent to the second address.

callBlock.who: Virginia M. — past client, two listing-alert opens nine days apart, and the CRM has never logged a single contact
callBlock.why: ⭐ TWO OPENS NINE DAYS APART IS A PATTERN, NOT A STRAY CLICK. Her record shows the alert sent and opened around 10 PM Friday, and the sweep logged another open twelve days before that. Four site visits, five listing views, average view price $323,000, and the CRM tags her intent as both seller and buyer. 🔴 THE PART THAT SHOULD BOTHER YOU: last interaction reads NONE. The CRM has no logged contact with her ever — while Gmail shows you closed her purchase in June 2017 and checked in twice after, and her husband wrote back "give us a heads up when you're back this way and we can give you the tour." That invitation is eight years old and was never taken up. ⚠️ ONE FACT TO NOT GET WRONG ON THE CALL: her one transaction has been treated as a Birmingham address and it is not — it is a lake condo in a different county, so any equity number built off a Birmingham appreciation table is wrong for that asset. Ask, don't assert. ⚠️ The do-not-call flag on her record attaches to a third line only; mobile and home are clear.

callBlock.who: Keith T. — your own note says "wants to discuss selling" and nobody has ever emailed him
callBlock.why: ⭐ THE BEST UNWORKED AT-BAT ON THE BOARD, AND THE TASK TEXT IS YOURS, NOT MACHINE NOISE — "Call!! Wants to discuss selling see notes," dated last December and roughly eight months overdue. ⚠️ A DEDUPE ACROSS BOTH ALIASES ON A 400-DAY WINDOW FOUND ZERO EMAILS TO HIM, EVER. The only activity on the record is your own note last November: "sent mailer." So the intent was logged, a mailer went out, and then eight months of nothing. ⚠️ TWO HONEST CAVEATS BEFORE YOU DIAL: the CRM has his intent as BUYER while your task says selling — one of the two is wrong and only the call settles it — and the property scores low to sell. This is an at-bat, not a layup. ⭐ But it is a free at-bat on a record that has never once been worked, and anything he told you in November may already have happened. No email was drafted deliberately: eight months of silence is a call, not a first email.
